chunks.l2:
[svab-p01-v02] I praise the highest Śiva — sick with no possession by any creed, to be known only by the feeling of the self, dwelling in himself.

[svab-p01-v03] Bow, let there be bow, to Śambhu — smasher of the net of fancies and their floods, standing past even the highest bliss.

[svab-p01-v04] Victorious are Śambhu's feet: they teach the wandering world to tell the real from the sham, and wake the knowledge that frees.

[svab-p01-v05] Mind, thought, ego, breaths, the senses' subtle fuel and life — all turn back when they see the one worth worshipping, whom we worship.

[svab-p01-v06] I bow — I — to pure awareness: the only knife that cuts the heart's knot of 'mine' and 'I', that swallowed throbbing and its stillness both.
chunks.sanskrit: aśeṣadarśanāveśaviśeṣādhivivarjitam / svasaṃvedanasaṃvedyaṃ svasthaṃ vande paraṃ śivam nirastakalpanājālavikalpaughavighātine / namo 'stu paramānandapadātītāya śambhave jayanty apārasaṃsārasārāsāravibhāgadāḥ / kaivalyajñānasaṃbodhahetavaś śambhavāṅghrayaḥ mano buddhir ahaṃ prāṇās tanmātrendriyajīvanam / yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinivartante tam upāsyam upāsmahe mamāham iti hṛdgranthicchedanaikakṛpāṇikām / spandāspandakṛtagrāsāṃ naumy ahaṃ śuddhasaṃvidam vyapadeśavihīnasya tattvasya kathanaṃ katham / svasaṃvedanasadyuktyā gamyate yadi kenacit jñānayogopadeśena yasya nāśvāsa āntaraḥ / samāśvāsavihīnatvāt kathaṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ phalam upeyaprāptyupāyo 'yaṃ svabodhe jāgarūkatā / svabodhajāgarūkatvān nirvibhāgā sthitir muneḥ upāyo nāparaḥ kaścit svasattānugamād ṛte / tām evānusaran yogī svastho yaḥ sa sukhī bhavet

chunks.l2:
[svab-p02-v11] From noticing your own notions, from holding to pure knowing, from winning the highest joy — the sage grows one solid mass of waking.

[svab-p02-v12] Grip your notions still, and power comes to rest in the powerful; their oneness is what yogis are after.

[svab-p02-v13] Know your own form, drop the veil of principles, scatter the cause of striving — then, tradition says, you are called free.

[svab-p02-v14] With a fully wakened mind, hold to waking alone — until, by your own strength, you stand in yourself, alone.
chunks.sanskrit: svasaṃkalpaparāmarśād viśuddhajñānasaṃśrayāt / paramāhlādalābhāc ca bodhaikaghanatā muneḥ nigṛhīte svasaṃkalpe śakteḥ śaktimati sthitiḥ / śaktiśaktimator aikyam ity upeyaṃ ca yoginām prāpte svarūpavijñāne santyakte tattvakañcuke / udyogakāraṇe kīrṇe muktaḥ sa kila kathyate bodhamātre grahaḥ kāryaḥ suprabuddhena cetasā / tāvad yāvat svasāmarthyāt svaniṣṭhaḥ kevalo bhavet sarvadā suprabuddhas san paśyaty ātmānam ātmanā / draṣṭuḥ svarūpasaṃsthasya kim anyad avaśiṣyate sadaiva suprabuddhatvam etāvan manasaḥ kṣayaḥ / tatkṣayād yogināṃ samyaksākṣātkāro bhavaty alam paryāvṛttaḥ svasaṃvittau vartate yas tv abhedataḥ / sa samrāḍ yogayuktānām ajñānadhvāntabhāskaraḥ svarūpānubhavāhlādadaśātītendusaṃsthitiḥ / avāptavyaṃ kim astīha kṣīṇāntaḥkaraṇasya me svaparijñaptiviśrāntī sudṛḍhe yasya susphuṭe / tasya vṛttivimuktasya bhavet kevalatācirāt

chunks.l2:
[svab-p03-v20] For yogis grounded in themselves, whose single mind sweeps aside the traces of grasping and the grasped — fortune's release is easy.

[svab-p03-v21] Rest in my own form I have won, my sorrows ended, the split of grasped and grasper broken — I stand firm, abiding as I am.

[svab-p03-v22] Whether up and about or gathered inward, whoever wins that nondual, wakened taste of his own nature knows what is real.

[svab-p03-v23] For one whose self-standing never slips in any state — what can the squabbles of scripture-rangers do to him?

[svab-p03-v24] His self freed from the delusion brewed of real and unreal notions — he lives on among people, fear gone, always a yogi.
chunks.sanskrit: grāhyagrahaṇasaṃskāratiraskāraikacetasām / yogināṃ svātmaniṣṭhānāṃ mokṣalakṣmīr na durlabhā labdhā svarūpaviśrāntir nirvṛttā kleśasantatiḥ / grāhyagrāhakatā bhagnā svarūpastho' smi saṃsthitaḥ abhedabodhasaṃbodhasvarūpānubhavasthitim / vyutthitaḥ sanniruddho vā labhate yaḥ sa tattvavit yasya sarvāsv avasthāsu svasthitir naiva lupyate / tasya kiṃ nāma kurvanti śāstrabhramaṇavibhramāḥ vigalitasadasadvikalpasadasadbhramajanitamohamuktātmā / jīvann api janamadhye vigatabhayaḥ sarvadā yogī nirastakaraṇo yena samādhiḥ sevitaḥ sakṛt / paraḥ sākṣātkṛtas tena caritārthena yoginā ahamātmany asambhinnaḥ saṃgṛhya svaprayatnataḥ / prabuddhaḥ syāt svaniṣṭhaḥ san yāvat sādāśivadyutiḥ nirastasarvārthaniraṃśavṛttir jñānī sakṛt svātmani labdhalābhaḥ / samyaṅnibodhaikaparaḥ svaniṣṭhaḥ svakañcukaṃ hanta jahāti yogī vāganubhavasadyuktir yasyāsti nirantaraṃ svasaṃvittau / tasyopadeśakaraṇaṃ yuktaṃ śiṣyeṣu bodhanaṃ samyak

chunks.l2:
[svab-p04-v29] From wanting nothing, from self-waking, from dropping hope and pride, from cutting the road of real-and-unreal — no taking of a body again.

[svab-p04-v30] Inner sense at peace, fancies thinned, delighting in the gain of his own form, drunk on the nectar of tasting himself — he goes to freedom, his work done.

[svab-p04-v31] So, for reaching the goal — stainless, lighting consciousness, true, mother of freedom's rise — I have told the perfection of self-waking.

[svab-p04-v32] This teaching can make even one who never won enough, and free him from doubt's fault — with such doubtless teaching, what business has the much-chanting scholar?

[svab-p04-v33] All-blessing maker, wildfire to tangled deeds, shower of your own station, free of every notion, temple of all joy — to cut suffering's root I bow to the unmatchably lovely Śiva, taught from the guru's mouth.
chunks.sanskrit: nairvāsanyāt svasaṃbodhāt tyāgād āśābhimānayoḥ / sadasatpadavicchedān na punar vigrahagrahaḥ āśvastāntaḥkaraṇaḥ kṣīṇavikalpaḥ svarūpalābharataḥ / svānubhavāmṛtatṛptaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti caritārthaḥ ittham upeyaprāptau vigatamalā citprakāśikā satyā / kaivalyabhūtijananī svabodhasiddhir mayā gaditā yenopadeśena nalabdhalābho bhavaty alaṃ saṃśayadoṣamuktaḥ / tenopadeśena nasaṃśayena kiṃ nāma kuryād bahuśāstrapāṭhī aśeṣakṛtamaṅgalaṃ vividhakarmadāvānalaṃ svarūpapadadarśakaṃ sakalakalpanāvarjitam / samastasukhamandiraṃ vividhaduḥkhamūlacchide namāmy asamasundaraṃ gurumukhopadiṣṭaṃ śivam
